findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition removes width/height API
findings.body: app/models/optimized_image.rb defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as (from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and again at line 149 as (from,to,dimensions,opts). In Ruby the second definition overwrites the first. Any existing caller using the 5-argument form will now get ArgumentError (5 for 3..4) and thumbnail generation breaks. The PR intended to add a new overload but instead deleted the old contract.

findings.title: Stale filesize passed to Upload after in-place downsize
findings.body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb downsizes the file in place on disk but then calls Upload.create_for with tempfile.size captured from the original Ruby file object. If ImageMagick rewrites/replaces the path, the open Tempfile descriptor still reports the old large size. Validation in the Upload model that uses the passed size will then reject the upload as too large even though the file on disk is now small, defeating the feature, or store an incorrect filesize in the database.

findings.title: In-place convert with same source/dest and unchecked failure
findings.body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%"...) in a loop without checking the return value. Reading and writing the same path with `convert src[0] ... dst` risks truncating/corrupting the file if the converter truncates the output before reading completes. On failure the file size never shrinks but the loop still retries 5 times wasting CPU and then proceeds to create the upload with a corrupt/oversize file.

findings.title: Client validation hardcodes 10MB ignoring site settings
findings.body: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js replaced Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] and max_image_size_kb with hardcoded 10*1024 in validateUploadedFile and displayErrorForUpload. Attachments and images now share the same 10MB client limit regardless of max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb settings. Admins who lowered limits will see client allow uploads the server rejects, and admins who raised limits above 10MB will see client incorrectly reject allowed files.

findings.title: Animated downsize passes percentage to gifsicle --resize-fit
findings.body: app/models/optimized_image.rb downsize_instructions_animated delegates to resize_instructions_animated which builds `gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}`. The new caller in uploads_controller passes dimensions as "80%". gifsicle expects WxH geometry, not a percentage, so animated GIF downsizing will fail, return false, and the retry loop in the controller will spin 5 times without ever shrinking the GIF.
